item.title: 法国银行被盗走 1.18 亿欧元
item.description: 法国国民互助信贷银行（Crédit Mutuel Arkéa）被黑客通过欺诈性交易盗走 1.18 亿欧元。被盗走的钱随后被转移到多个加密货币账号。该银行证实遭到网络攻击，但尚未证实 1.18 亿欧元的数字，只是表示攻击已得到控制，客户不会遭受任何经济损失。国民互助信贷银行暂停了其应用的部分转账功能。

item.title: Vance blames Iran war for GOP's midterm losses in social media post
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance blamed Republicans’ sweeping midterm losses on the war with Iran on Wednesday, arguing that voters who backed President Donald Trump in 2024 turned against the Republican Party over the conflict.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance wrote in a lengthy social media post.

The remarks represent a striking acknowledgment from the vice president that the administration’s handling of the Iran conflict has become a political liability for Republicans, even as his boss has defended the approach to the war.

Vance also suggested that Republicans who supported the war should concede the political costs rather than look for alternative explanations for the Tuesday results.

“To the people who are pissed off and want to say, ‘I told you so’: you’re right, you did tell us so,” he wrote in his lengthy post. “Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview.”

Vance’s assessment of the GOP wreckage quickly gained praise from some close to Trump. Donald Trump Jr., the president’s eldest son, reposted Vance’s autopsy, adding: “Every word of this is 💯💯💯.”

When asked about the post Wednesday afternoon, Trump said “I know how [Vance] feels about it. I think it was fine. I thought it was good.”

He did not answer whether he knew Vance was going to make the post.

"I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term," Trump said of Vance's claims. "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again because long term, it's the only answer."

The vice president argued that Republican turnout was strong Tuesday but that many voters who supported his ticket two years ago instead cast ballots for Democrats.

“Our voters did show up,” Vance wrote. “But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.”

Vance pointed to four answers an unnamed trusted pollster gave him about what voters said would win their votes back: ending the war, focusing on cost of living, putting “America First” and changing the U.S. relationship to Israel.

Vance — who was initially one of the least supportive members of the administration on the war in Iran but ultimately took on a public-facing role in negotiating failed peace deals over the summer — said that people might continue to argue about whether the war was a worthwhile price to pay for “losing the Senate for the next 6 years” but that they should start from acknowledging it was, in fact, the reason.

“Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest,” he wrote. “But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

The president seemed less willing to back down on Iran in a phone call with POLITICO on Tuesday night. Trump said he was hearing that the midterm losses could be related to oil prices driven higher by the conflict, but that he remained “totally convinced” that using military force in Iran was the “absolutely correct” decision.

“And it continues to be,” Trump said.

Trump also didn’t rule out continued strikes after the midterms.

“We're going to take a look,” Trump said Tuesday night. “I think if we see any opportunity to do one thing or another, we're going to do what's best for this country.”

The president did rule out the use of nuclear weapons on the country, speculation that recently made the rounds after being raised by conservative commentator Tucker Carlson, who has sharply criticized the administration’s interventions in Iran and its support of Israel.

In his early analysis of the results, Vance also appeared to anticipate and try to preempt an internal Republican fight over how the party should respond to its losses, particularly on the administration’s hardline immigration stance and use of ICE. “Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty,” Vance said. “I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement — by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you.”

Vance, who first ran for the Senate in 2022 before becoming Trump’s vice president, is a known 2028 presidential contender who Trump openly muses could take up the MAGA mantle.

But both Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the other top contender in Trump’s administration, have been publicly tied to the unpopular war in Iran through their continued roles in negotiations and policy decisions.

The president’s continued support for the war sets up a headwind for the potential candidates in 2028 — a circumstance Vance acknowledged and sought to get ahead of on Wednesday morning with a call to action for voters to join him in turning policy around.

“To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country,” Vance wrote.

CORRECTION: An earlier version of this report misstated Vance's electoral history.This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/04/jd-vance-iran-war-midterms-01148838

item.title: 专访：民主党赢得中期选举如何影响美国的对华政策？
item.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/专访：民主党赢得中期选举如何影响美国的对华政策？/a-79857005
item.description:
德正
2026-11-04T15:48:27.045Z
民主党横扫参众两院，特朗普沦为“跛脚鸭”？

德国之声：中国对美国中期选举结果反应谨慎。外交部发言人毛宁在例行记者会上被问及对美国中期选举的看法时表示，中期选举是美国内政。中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好落实好两国元首重要共识。您怎么看这样的表态？

费多丽教授：首先，中国评价美国选举结果态度审慎是非常典型的做法。他们通常不会明确表达倾向，而是往往以“这是内政”作为回应。不过，“中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好落实好两国元首重要共识”这种措辞显示，中方预料到，外界可能会认为中国对选举结果会不那么满意，因为他们刚刚才和特朗普达成了安排。换句话说，他们认为民主党人，或者很多人认为民主党人，现在会采取更进一步的行动。因此中方强调，“我们仍然愿意合作。”

相关图集：从习近平四次访美 看中美关系近年的发展脉络

习近平专机降落华盛顿（2026）：2026年9月23日当地时间傍晚，习近平访美专机在离白宫约20公里的安德鲁斯联合基地降落。这是习近平担任中国国家主席后第四次访问美国。
特朗普总统携夫人接机（2026）：特朗普携夫人梅拉尼娅亲自赶往安德鲁斯基地接机。这是11年来首次有美国总统在这里迎接外国客人。上一次是在2015年，由时任总统奥巴马迎接教宗方济各。
习近平：中美应该成为伙伴而不是对手（2026）：此次访问是对特朗普5月访华的回访。抵达华府后，习近平发表书面谈话，强调中美“应该成为伙伴而不是对手。” 奏响美国国歌时，两架 B-1B“枪骑兵”（B-1B Lancer）战略轰炸机从头顶轰鸣而过，引发各方多种解读。
小范围会谈：谈及台湾了吗？（2026）：习近平在致辞时说，未来5年邀请10万名美国青少年前往中国交流，两只大熊猫落户亚特兰大动物园。但中美掌舵人小范围讨论了什么、敲定了什么，外界并不知晓。有关台湾问题，中国外交部的新闻稿写道，习近平对特朗普表示，希望美方坚持反对台独的正确立场。
大佬精英云集的国宴：谈历史、讲友谊 （2026） ：白宫数天前发布信息：第一夫人梅拉尼娅亲自领衔筹备国宴。主宾轮流致辞，谈历史、讲友谊，敏感话题一律不提。许多美国科技和商界大佬应邀到场，但中国企业家却集体缺席。习近平再提，”美国再次伟大“和“中国民族复兴”并行不悖。
在海湖庄园 习近平同特朗普首次见面（2017）：2017年4月6日，习近平抵达美国佛罗里达州，与特朗普在他的海湖庄园举行会晤。这是他们二人首次见面。有专家认为，二人都在摸底对方，建立工作个人关系。共进晚餐时，特朗普告知美国正向叙利亚发射“战斧”巡航导弹，这让客人近距离感受到美国的军事力量。
为今后互动奠定了基础（2017）：中美双方当时在贸易、朝鲜、南海、台湾等问题上存在很大分歧。但此次会面为今后的互动奠定了基础。特朗普接受了习近平的邀请，于同年11月访问了中国。双方同意建立高级别对话机制。不过数月之后，特朗普打响影响至今的中美贸易战。
习近平首次对美国进行国事访问（2015）：2015年9月22日至28日，习近平第一次以国家主席身份正式访问美国。但第一站不是华盛顿、而是西雅图，他走访了波音和微软等美国巨头公司。
副总统拜登接机、奥巴马设晚宴（2015）：奥巴马夫妇设晚宴欢迎到访的习近平，两人的会谈持续了两个半小时，涉及话题很广，尤其是网络安全与网络间谍、南海等问题。习近平表示无意推动南海的军事化。9月25日发表了新的中美元首气候变化联合声明。
习近平主席首次访美 低调进行（2013）：2013年6月刚上任中国国家主席的习近平借出访拉美之机，停留加州安纳伯格庄园，同刚刚开始第二任期的总统奥巴马举行会晤。这不是一次国事访问。包括怎样构建“新型大国关系”，两国首脑进行了8小时会晤，结束时没有新闻发布会，也没有在机场发表声明。
美方的关切、习近平的宽广太平洋（2013）：中美双方均有最高层的核心人物参加加州会谈。会后，美国国家安全顾问多尼隆（Tom Donilon）告知，奥巴马对习表示，网络安全问题、美国知识产权继续直接遭到窃取问题，将成为经济关系中十分困难的事项，并阻碍双边关系发挥出全部的潜力。习近平则表示，宽广的太平洋有足够空间容纳中美两个大国。

德国之声：中国看来有些担心中期选举的这一结果可能会对中美关系产生一些影响。那么您认为影响会有多大？

费多丽教授：根据近年来的经验，中国政府担心民主党人对华的态度会比特朗普更具批判性。特朗普被指折服于习近平的领导才能，在这一层面上建立了不一样的关系，因此在处理对华关系方面对抗性有所降低。但必须指出的是，美国在特朗普执政期间也对中国实施了制裁措施。虽然他们今年还没有向台湾交付武器，但也并没有真正对中国采取友好，或者和解的态度。情况非常复杂。可以说，过去这些年，无论谁入主白宫，在对华问题上都相对一致。拜登并没有完全推翻特朗普第一任期对华政策，特朗普也没有推翻拜登的做法。当然，他们的优先事项不同，处理方式也截然不同。但从根本上讲，共和党人和民主党人都认为中国是主要挑战，需要采取战略性应对措施。

德国之声：具体而言，中期选举后，美国在外交、贸易和关税政策上可能有不同的做法吗？

费多丽教授：就外交政策，包括贸易政策和关税政策而言，现任总统很明显不怎么遵循国会的建议。因此，我们不知道，民主党主导国会后，是否真的有能力通过国会正常的、合法的、既定的程序来阻止特朗普在这些领域采取独立行动。或许可以提起诉讼，但这需要时间。所以，目前情况很复杂。这不仅关系对华政策。

观察人士认为，民主党可能会试图对白宫施加更大的压力。但实际上——正如有人所说——特朗普现在这个所谓的“跛脚鸭”，在接下来的两年内，也可能变成一只愤怒的鸭子，想要强行推进某些事情。因此，我们对接下来会怎样其实一无所知。我们可以看看月底的APEC峰会上发生什么。我相信习近平和特朗普的会晤仍将按计划举行。或许我们能从中窥见事态的发展方向。我认为我们不会立即看到巨大的变化，短期内美国的对华政策不会有大的变化。

德国之声：您刚才提到台湾，在这方面美国的政策会有什么改变吗？

费多丽教授：我不是台湾问题专家，但如果我理解没错的话，在特朗普执政期间，原计划今年运往台湾的武器已被暂停。理论上讲，可以想象民主党人会更加努力地推动对这批武器的交付。但努力归努力，最终是否能促成此事就完全是另一回事了。

德国之声：您能简单总结一下特朗普执政两年来，中美的地位和力量对比发生什么变化吗？

费多丽教授：中国的确也受了特朗普政府制裁的打击，但我认为，目前最关键的是，世界其他地区，尤其是全球南方国家，认为特朗普政府在各种领域的政策都难以预测，很难知道特朗普政府下一步会做什么，想要什么，以及它的声明有多可靠。这包括贸易战，但也延伸到伊朗战争和类似问题。特朗普政府的这种等级森严且难以预测性，导致了中国形象和实力的普遍提升。但与此同时，也有另外一种趋势。在欧洲，我们也感受到了在美国蔓延的对中国的恐惧。这种恐惧正在欧洲日益扩散。

不过，如果我们暂时忽略这些因素，只关注特朗普及其政府在国际政治中的行为，那么中国无疑已经从中受益，中国在世界上的地位似乎得到了加强。

至于特朗普对中国的经济政策，中国现任领导层可以把功劳归于自己，说我们对特朗普的反应是正确的，我们挺身对抗他，展现了实力，事实证明这很有效，正因为如此，特朗普现在才相对放过了我们。有些人从心理层面分析，认为特朗普确实喜欢强人，所以他才会在某种程度上欣赏中国。不过，涉及实际的贸易冲突、安全冲突、信息和虚假信息问题等等，中国也并非完全占据上风。大家都在摸索，试图找到解决这些冲突的方法。

此外，中国经济目前面临着诸多问题，包括一些需求方面的问题。近期股市的疲软也被解读为对人工智能能力缺乏信心。中国经济目前似乎正处于低迷状态，但这种情况我们现在在美国也看到了。但这些问题并非主要由中美双边关系决定，中国目前面临的困境也并非出口市场之类的问题，而是与中国的经济政策、政策的实施方式以及优先事项的设定密切相关。

德国维尔茨堡大学费多丽教授（Dr. Doris Fischer）

德国之声：美国对中国商品，比如电动汽车等商品进口有很多限制，这样的趋势还会继续吗？

费多丽教授：我不认为国会会向白宫施压，要求对中国实施更多贸易限制，至少不会以太多商品从中国流入美国为由。如果真有什么动向，那也只会是出于安全方面的考虑。但我认为他们不会把这作为首要任务。民主党首先需要理顺内部事务，弄清楚如何应对这种新局面，如何稳定现在这股浪潮，从而在两年后再次赢得总统大选。而且国会现在是否真的拥有影响力并能带来巨大变革，比如在关税政策方面，我对此表示怀疑。如果主要目的是抑制通货膨胀，他们也许会说，或许我们应该降低关税。但通货膨胀当然也很大程度上受能源价格的影响，而关税对能源价格没有影响。所以情况很复杂。我预计民主党人需要一些时间来站稳脚跟，适应他们的新角色。

item.title: Trump avoids discussing GOP midterm losses as he tours White House ballroom
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump reacted Wednesday to Republicans' midterm election losses by showing off the White House ballroom he's building as he demonstrated the kind of detached behavior that voters around the country said was a key reason they opted to punish his party.

In an extraordinary scene, Trump summoned reporters to the hulking construction site that he demolished the East Wing to make room for and the Republican president spoke for nearly 20 minutes about minute building details. He did not mention his party losing control of Congress after defeats in some of the country's deepest GOP strongholds, including Texas and South Carolina, or voter concerns about the high cost of living and federal corruption that helped cause the election losses.

“This has been a structure the likes of which has never been seen anywhere,” Trump said, speaking into a microphone that sent loud feedback echoing around the cavernous space.

He talked at length about how the ballroom would be the ”safest place in Washington" upon completion, stretching five stories underground and featuring a cut of marble that he called “a vein that people have been after for 50 years.”

“We have large staircases coming from the kitchen. If I put the kitchen on top, you would lose three walls, because a kitchen takes about 30% of the space,” Trump said of his choice to make the ballroom's kitchen subterranean.

“It’s going to be top of the line," he added.

This is not what presidents normally talk about the day after an election

Presidents usually speak with reporters the day after the midterms. It's normal for those whose party endured big losses to shoulder publicly at least part of the responsibility.

But not Trump.

He began the day with a schedule that showed only private meetings, then suggested he had decided at the last minute to invite the press to watch as the final steel beam — topped with a small evergreen tree symbolizing growth and luck — was hoisted into place on the ballroom roof.

Trump signed the beam with a marker during the ceremony, writing “Love!” followed by his name in supersize letters.

His appearance came after midterm voters said they thought the president was focused on the wrong issues. About two-thirds of voters said Trump does not have the right priorities, according to The AP Voter Poll, and the overwhelming majority of these voters supported Democratic House candidates.

The post-midterm ceremony might also reinforce voter concerns about whether Trump, 80, is up for the rigors of the presidency.

Biden dropped out of his reelection race in 2024 after a disastrous debate with Trump, who even today frequently mocks Biden's mental and physical acuity.

Trump seeks to shift blame for the midterms

Trump eventually took questions at the ballroom site and attempted to duck responsibility for the broad Republican losses. He insisted he didn't lead the party into an Election Day drubbing despite staging a flurry of rallies where he implored supporters to pretend that he was on the ballot.

"If I were on the ballot I would have won,” Trump insisted.

He said campaign rallies in mostly Republican states or conservative parts of more closely divided ones featured enthusiastic crowds “but we weren’t able to transfer love to the candidates.”

The beam-raising was not his first baffling political moment this week. On Monday, Trump gave his closing message of the midterm cycle in a long speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, shining a spotlight at a pivotal time on a project marred by algae, leaks and delays.

“I heard it was a very good speech, got great reviews,” he said on Wednesday.

Ducking responsibility is common with Trump

An Associated Press analysis of the 39 Trump speeches and rallies that Trump staged between Sept. 1 and Election Day showed the president used phrasing suggesting he was on the ballot in 30 of them. In some addresses he returned to the subject more than once, though, meaning there were at least 40 instances where he appealed to voters to engage in that bit of make-believe.

But as the extent of his party's defeat became apparent on election night, Trump was deflecting blame.

“I don’t like to consider it a defeat for me. I wasn’t on the ballot,” he told Fox News Channel. Voters, he said, just “didn’t like the candidates” on the ballot. The Voter Poll suggests Trump himself was a drag on GOP politicians and that in some races, candidates were seen as too supportive of the unpopular president.

Trump has a long history of passing the buck, on issues large and small, especially when there are ballot-box failures.

After Republicans lost the House in the 2018 midterms during Trump's first term, he blamed defeated members of his own party.

Utah Rep. Mia Love, who had tried to distance herself from him, “gave me no love, but then she lost. Too bad," the president said, while also mocking other losing lawmakers for not embracing him — Florida's Carlos Curbelo, Colorado's Mike Coffman, Virginia's Barbara Comstock, and Illinois' Peter Roskam.

That's in contrast to how Democrat Barack Obama described his party's losses in 2010 as “a shellacking" or Republican George W. Bush described Democratic victories in the 2006 midterms as “a thumping.”

But Trump, known for defying all kinds of presidential norms, began laying the groundwork for avoiding blame this cycle well before balloting began.

He told Punchbowl News in August that voters were angry at Republicans “but they’re not angry at me.”

The president posted on his social media site last month that should Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton lose — and he did — "it will be because of WEAK and INEFFECTIVE Political Hacks like John Cornyn and Karl Rove.” That's despite Trump's risky endorsement of scandal-marred Paxton in the primary over incumbent Cornyn, who first got to the Senate in 2002 and was considered the safer bet. Rove is a political strategist who helped Bush win the White House.

Also losing Tuesday was Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, a longtime Trump ally.

Trump posted on social media that if Abbott “hadn’t become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost," suggesting the governor had backed away from his staunchly conservative credentials and become “Republican in Name Only.”

__

Associated Press writers Amelia Thomson DeVeaux, Linley Sanders, Josh Boak and Aaron Kessler contributed to this report.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-ducking-blame-republican-losses-165128236.html

item.title: 韩国游戏 PC 启动器被植入恶意代码
item.description: 韩国游戏《胜利女神：新的希望（NIKKE）》的 PC 启动器被植入恶意代码。恶意代码是通过纂改 Level Infinite CDN 分发的四个官方 JavaScript 文件实现的，篡改发生于 2026 年 9 月 27 日前后，攻击则始于 2026 年 10 月 23 日到 11 月 3 日，在此期间打开 PC 启动器的用户可能会被植入木马。恶意程序会窃取浏览器保存的密码、Windows 凭据管理器信息、SSH 密钥以及云服务或 AI 服务的访问令牌，还能窃取 28 种基于浏览器的加密货币钱包数据、执行任意命令、读取文件以及屏幕截图。攻击期间打开过启动器的玩家可以打开游戏文件夹，搜寻 debug.log，打开该文件后寻找 k2f_chan，如果找到且显示 registered，那么最好立即卸载游戏并用杀毒软件进行扫描。

item.title: AMD 营收预计将首次超过英特尔
item.description: AMD 周二公布了 2026 财年第三季度财报，营收同比增长 45% 达到 134 亿美元。其中数据中心业务贡献了 85 亿美元营收同比增长 97%。客户端与游戏业务部门的营收下滑了 8% 降至 37 亿美元。作为 AMD 在 x86 市场的主要竞争对手，英特尔下一季度营收预计为 150-160 亿美元，其增长几乎停滞。相比下 AMD 预计下一季度营收将达到约 170 亿美元。如果达到这一目标，这将标志着 AMD 营收首次超过英特尔。

item.title: Trump Media falls to an all-time low as Democrats take back Congress
item.description:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump’s social media company and meme coin both plunged after Democrats won a decisive victory in the midterm elections, dinging the multibillion-dollar fortune of a president whose slew of new business ventures became a defining feature of his second term.

Most Read from Bloomberg

  • Morgan Stanley Offers $2.3 Billion Debt for Dell Family Deal
  • Democrats Sweep to Control of Congress in Rebuke of Trump
  • What the Democrats’ Sweep of Congress Means for Trump
  • Democrat El-Sayed Wins Michigan Race in Boost to Progressives
  • Democrats Clinch Huge Wins on Inflation Anger, Trump Fatigue

Trump Media & Technology Group Corp., the parent company of social media platform Truth Social, touched an all-time low of $5.03 on Wednesday. $TRUMP, the virtual token that Trump introduced days before his second inauguration, slid more than 10% in the past 24 hours, according to data provider CoinMarketCap. 

The simultaneous drop in both assets — which trade heavily on retail speculation — signals investors may be anxious about the implications of the election for the businesses with links to the president, which are now expected to receive fresh congressional oversight. 

For months, Democrats have signaled their appetite to pursue investigations into the president and his family’s business interests if they prevail in either chamber, leaving any company connected to the first family as a potential target.

“LAWYER UP,” Robert Garcia, the California Democrat in line to chair the House Oversight Committee, posted on social media as the results rolled in on Tuesday night.

The businesses account for meaningful wealth for the first family. Trump’s stake in the social media company, which he holds through a trust controlled by his eldest son Donald Trump Jr, is worth about $600 million; the meme coin business accounts for about $83 million, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. 

Trump shunned decades of norms for American presidents, drawing rebuke from the left for profiting from cryptocurrency ventures and business interests that bear his name while in office. 

When the New York Times asked the president earlier this year about conflicts of interest in his second term, he said, “I found out that nobody cared.” The White House has maintained that there are no conflicts of interests involving the president’s business ventures.

Yet polling ahead of the midterms showed that government corruption, broadly, was a significant concern for voters. A Fox News poll found 60% of voters were extremely worried about government corruption, while a Gallup survey showed Americans’ perceptions of government corruption in the US hit their highest level in 20 years, with 89% of respondents calling it widespread.

  • 7 Brew, Gen Z’s Anti-Starbucks, Is on an Expansion Spree
  • Texas Pays Online School Empire for Kids Who Don’t Show Up

item.title: 荷兰安世向中国母公司索赔20亿美元 跨国经营体系陷入分裂
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

荷兰半导体制造商安世（Nexperia）11月3日宣布，已向荷兰法院起诉中国母公司闻泰科技、创始人张学政及相关中国实体，要求赔偿超过20亿美元，指控中方违反内部协议、建立独立供应链，并与原集团形成直接竞争。

据路透社报道，安世认为，中方相关行为严重损害公司业务及利益。闻泰科技否认全部指控，表示尚未收到法院正式传票，将聘请海外律师应诉。

这场争端始于2025年荷兰政府介入安世经营。荷兰法院随后暂停张学政的管理职务，并将闻泰持有的大部分股东投票权交由独立管理人行使。安世中国业务此后与荷兰总部发生严重分歧，原有跨国供应链逐渐分裂。

中国政府曾对安世中国相关产品实施出口限制，导致欧洲汽车制造商面临芯片供应短缺。虽然中荷政府后来调整干预措施，双方经营纠纷仍未解决。

目前闻泰仍持有安世股权，但已失去主要经营控制权。双方分别在中国及荷兰展开诉讼，涉及公司控制权、内部协议履行及巨额损害赔偿，最终责任仍待法院认定。

关键词: 
荷兰

item.title: 法国血库遭网络攻击 冷冻设备被设定至110度
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

法国国家血液中心（EFS）11月4日证实，其冷冻设备服务供应商日前遭到网络攻击，导致三个血液储存设施的监控及控制系统受到影响。黑客将部分原本设定为摄氏零下30度的冷冻设备，远程修改为摄氏110度，引发对血液制品储存安全的担忧。

据法新社及法国《鸭鸣报》报道，攻击发生于11月2日，受影响设施储存着血液样本，以及供输血和药品生产使用的血浆。攻击者通过供应商的系统修改设备运行参数，试图干扰正常低温储存。

法国国家血液中心表示，独立监控与警报机制及时发现异常，工作人员随即采取保护措施。尽管设备设定值遭到篡改，实际库温并未升至110度，事件没有造成血液制品损失，也未对患者健康产生影响。

此次事件显示，网络攻击不仅能够窃取资料和资金，还可能通过远程控制系统干扰医疗设施的物理设备。独立监控及现场应急措施在此次事件中发挥了关键作用。

关键词: 
法国
血库
网络攻击
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 美国10月民间就业增加8.6万人 薪资增长超预期
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国自动数据处理公司（ADP）11月4日公布的报告显示，10月美国民间企业新增就业8.6万人，高于市场预期，显示劳动力市场仍保持温和增长。9月份新增就业人数经修正后同样为8.6万人。

报告显示，服务业是就业增长主要动力，其中贸易、运输及公用事业新增3.9万个职位，教育及医疗服务业增加2.8万个，餐饮旅游业增加1.9万个。专业及商业服务业则减少2.7万个职位，制造业减少1000个。

薪资方面，民间企业员工底薪同比增长3.2%，包括奖金、加班费及工时变化在内的总薪资增长4.7%。其中，转职员工的总薪资增幅达到7.6%，留任员工增长4.4%。

ADP首席经济学家理查森表示，各种规模的企业上月均有招聘活动，转职者除获得较高基本工资外，还受益于奖金、加班费及工时增加，推动薪资增长。

美国劳工部定于11月6日公布10月官方非农就业报告。由于统计方法不同，官方数据可能与ADP报告存在差异。

关键词: 
美国就业
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: California's billionaire tax is losing despite a nationwide backlash against the rich
item.description:
California's proposed billionaire tax appeared headed for defeat on Wednesday in one of the final verdicts from voters in an election week that saw a wave of anti-billionaire sentiment elsewhere.

The latest results on Wednesday afternoon showed California's Proposition 40 down by over 11 percentage points, with 60% of votes counted but the race not yet formally called.

The referendum would amend California's constitution and impose a one-time 5% tax on California residents and trusts with assets over $1 billion on Jan. 1, 2026. The revenue would primarily go toward healthcare, as well as food assistance and education.

Some assets, such as real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions, were excluded.

The measure was estimated to impact about 200 billionaires in the state. It faced fierce opposition from many in Big Tech and lost steam with voters as Election Day neared.

Google (GOOG, GOOGL) co-founder Sergey Brin was one of the measure's most vocal opponents. He contributed a reported $102 million to a political committee to fight the measure.

Other billionaires made detailed plans in case it passed. Meta (META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg told his board, according to a New York Times report, that they needed to take steps to shield him from the tax or he would publicly list his home in Palo Alto for sale.

The measure was also opposed by some Democrats, who argued it wouldn't work.

Outgoing California Gov. Gavin Newsom emerged as an opponent, arguing that billionaires would both dodge the tax and leave the state. He cited a report from the California Legislative Analyst's Office that estimated the measure might temporarily boost state revenues but could be an overall drag on regular income taxes and "would reduce state revenues by less than $1 billion per year."

Across the country, voters in red and blue states delivered verdicts on wealth inequality and the influence of the ultrarich. In Texas, where Elon Musk spent more than $200 million to keep the state's Senate seat in Republican hands, voters flipped the seat for Democrats and made clear their unease over AI data centers.

Tuesday's results also saw a series of wins by candidates who represent the Democratic Socialists of America, many of whom ran on explicitly anti-billionaire platforms. At least seven DSA members will take seats in Congress next year, as well as the mayors' offices of Los Angeles and Washington, D.C.

California voters were also weighing competing measures: Proposition 41 and Proposition 42, which were introduced by opponents of Proposition 40 to prevent the wealth tax from taking effect.

Proposition 42 would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets, and retirement holdings. It was on track to pass based on the latest results.

The wealth tax had support from progressives like Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Rep. Ro Khanna of California, who called the measure "the most important ballot initiative in America."

Khanna on Tuesday night acknowledged the measure's fading prospects, saying in a press conference, "I'm proud of our efforts wherever we end up [and] I am going to be right there, first in line supporting this in the next election cycle if it doesn't pass this one."

On Wednesday, Khanna wrote an op-ed for MS Now calling for a new federal tax on billionaires.

Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/californias-billionaire-tax-on-track-for-defeat-as-the-state-continues-to-count-votes-190840319.html

item.title: 'Lawyer up': Democrats prepare to investigate Trump after taking Congress
item.description:
Democrats in Congress gained the power Tuesday night to more forcefully investigate President Trump and rein in his agenda, setting up confrontations that are likely to define the final two years of his presidency.

As party leaders on Wednesday celebrated retaking the House and Senate, they vowed to put Trump and his administration on the defensive with subpoenas and hearings, a role that voters made clear they want them to play. But they also said the top priority would be the issue that swept them to power: making life more affordable.

“We are going to work hard to drive costs down with the president or without him, period,” Sen. Chuck Schumer, who is poised to become Senate majority leader, said at a news conference.

Schumer’s fellow New Yorker and the House Democratic leader, Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, echoed those priorities on CNN: “We ran on affordability, we won decisively on affordability, and now we have a responsibility to govern on affordability.”

With power split between the legislative and executive branches, to what degree Washington avoids gridlock will depend on how Trump wields his veto pen and how the Democrats negotiate with him — and how they follow through on pledges to investigate what they called a corrupt administration.

“Make no mistake, whenever Trump defies the will of the American people or the law, we will launch investigations, take him to court and entangle him in legislative razor wire,” Schumer said. “The days of Trump’s supplicate Senate are over.”

Read more: Democrats' historic rout was fueled by massive voter swing to the left

Trump, for his part, congratulated Democrats, but on Fox News said, “They are in control, but they’re really not in control. They can send over 50 different, great bills that they’re all excited about, and I send them back with a nice stamp veto.”

Trump added that he has “friends” in the Democratic Party and is willing to make deals. “I don’t want to be just sitting there for two years vetoing everything,” he said.

Schumer argued that the Democrats’ decisive victories show the president’s weakness and give them legislative leverage, and he warned Republicans against resisting their agenda.

“If they continue to embrace Trump, they are going to be following him right over the cliff, as this election has shown, and it will get even worse for them,” he said.

After four years out of power, House Democrats plan to carry out plans they have spent months mapping out — investigating the Trump family’s business dealings, allegedly corrupt deals by administration officials and suspected abuses by federal immigration agents.

In a sign of what is to come, Rep. Robert Garcia of Long Beach, the top Democrat on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, wrote on X: “LAWYER UP.”

Read more: 'Not a hit on me': Trump faults candidates and Fox News, not himself, for Republican losses

Democrats also intend to summon top Cabinet officials to testify on many hot-button issues, such as the war in Iran.

They could also bring oil, insurance, pharmaceutical and other industries under congressional scrutiny. That oversight tactic could help Democrats’ push to lower costs regardless of whether they can get Trump to sign legislation.

The Democrat majorities in both chambers are substantial. In the Senate, where Republicans held a 53-47 majority going into Tuesday, Democrats have won 54 seats to Republicans’ 44 as of Wednesday, according to Associated Press projections.

In the House, Republicans entered the election with 218 seats to Democrats’ 214. Now, Democrats have 237 seats, well past the 218 needed for a majority, and some races remain undecided.

The Senate majority hands Democrats the ability to block Trump’s judicial and other nominations — including appointments to the Supreme Court. Democrats do not have the numbers, however, to reach the two-thirds majority needed to override Trump’s veto.

The Democratic victory will also probably kick off a new chapter of the party’s tug-of-war over its identity. A group of insurgent progressives, several of them democratic socialists who defeated establishment-backed candidates in primaries, will join a caucus whose majority includes moderates from Republican-leaning districts.

Read more: Fears of election day interference fizzle, but federal war on voter fraud could continue

Holding together a caucus that stretches from democratic socialists to centrists is likely to be the first major test for Jeffries, who is poised to become speaker. Much of that balancing act could run through California, more than any other state. Its Democrats form the largest bloc in the new majority, and several are in line for powerful posts.

Among them is Garcia, who is in line to lead the Oversight Committee and vowed last month to investigate possible corruption by the Trump family and administration officials.

The committee, Garcia said, will also “focus on issues around the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and on corporate corruption. But our fourth major investigative area is going to be on the abuses of ICE and DHS.”

Garcia said that the committee has flagged more than 1,000 instances of “credible, verifiable abuses by federal immigration agents,” and that scrutinizing those examples will be a key part of the panel’s work in the coming months. He added that he also would like to look into white nationalist groups’ role in recruiting federal immigration agents.

As Democrats lay the groundwork for investigations, many in the party are wary of the most aggressive tool available to them: impeachment. Trump, the only president to have been impeached twice, has said it would be “very unfair” if Democrats move to impeach him a third time.

Some Democrats have floated impeachment as an option, but others argue it could distract from their affordability agenda.

Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, which plays a key role in the impeachment process, told MS NOW in August that Trump is “very eager” for Democrats to impeach him so he can mobilize his political base.

“We’re not going to play into the game,” he said.

item.title: NASA's 3,200-pound observatory met a fiery end after a failed rescue mission
item.description:
NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory met a fiery end on Wednesday morning, nearly 22 years after it launched to study the most powerful explosions in the universe.

Data from the US Space Force estimates the 3,200-pound spacecraft plunged into Earth’s atmosphere over Indonesia around 7:39 a.m. ET.

While most of the observatory was expected to burn up as it blazed through the thick inner band of Earth’s atmosphere, NASA predicted some pieces of the vehicle would survive.

It was not immediately clear whether any surviving debris hit land. Previously, NASA had predicted that the “risk of harm coming to anyone on Earth is unlikely, approximately 1 in 2,100.”

A risky reentry

If Swift were launched today, it would likely have to adhere to far stricter safety guidelines regarding end-of-life planning, according to The Aerospace Corporation, which is a federally funded research and development center.

Current orbital debris mitigation standards, which were updated in 2019, mandate that “uncontrolled reentries have an expected casualty of less than 1 in 10,000,” said Parker Wishik, a spokesperson for The Aerospace Corporation. He noted in an email that, in this context, “casualty” refers to “serious injury or death.”

While NASA has long known that Swift would likely have to make an unpredictable plunge back to Earth, the agency had hoped that a daring rescue mission launched in July could latch on and boost the Swift Observatory as atmospheric drag gradually pulled it from a once-stable orbit. It could have extended Swift’s operating life by a decade or more, but ultimately the effort failed. The spacecraft eventually dropped down to just 171 miles (275 kilometers) above the planet, and the observatory officially stopped gathering scientific data.

“At this point, the spacecraft was no longer able to compensate for the effects of the increased drag and entered safe mode,” NASA said in a news release.

A team of researchers at Penn State — NASA’s partner on the project and home to the observatory’s Mission Operations Center — sent the final kill-switch command to Swift on October 20.

unknown content item

-

Swift’s demise was hastened by an increase in solar activity over the past couple of years as the sun reached the peak of its 11-year cycle in 2024.

Intense flares and coronal mass ejections caused Earth’s atmosphere to expand, which intensified the drag on Swift, leading scientists to predict it would descend toward our planet this fall.

Arizona-based Katalyst Space Technologies scrambled to put together the last-ditch effort to stabilize the Swift observatory earlier this year, getting the rescue mission off the ground in only nine months. The company rapidly produced a spacecraft called LINK, which aimed to grapple the telescope and lift it back into a stable orbit. But the mission failed a few weeks after LINK’s launch in July as the satellite spun out of control in space before reaching the Swift observatory.

Another rescue attempt

As Swift’s fate was sealed, mission scientists slowly turned the telescope’s instruments back on to collect data and observations right up until the end. The instruments had been shut off for months to save power and mitigate how quickly the spacecraft sank out of orbit.

The Swift Observatory, which does not have an established observational replacement waiting in the wings, has served as an astrophysics multi-tool in low-Earth orbit since it launched in November 2004.

Named after fast-flying birds, the telescope could quickly pivot to observe blink-and-you-miss-it cosmic events such as flaring black holes. The telescope was originally designed to study the most powerful explosions in the universe, called gamma-ray bursts, but scientists have also used it to monitor other types of cosmic flashes as well as asteroids and comets.

Despite the failed attempt to rescue Swift, NASA has signaled it may try similar lifeline-extension missions for other valuable space-based instruments. Last week, the agency issued a solicitation — formally called a Request for Proposals or RFP — to commercial companies, asking how they might boost, service or otherwise prolong the life of the iconic Hubble Space Telescope.

NASA’s analysis shows that there’s a 10% chance Hubble will plunge out of orbit by 2032 and a 50% it will deorbit by 2033, according to the RFP. The beloved telescope, launched in 1990, has delivered some of the most recognizable images in astronomy and has transformed scientists’ understanding of the cosmos. There is no replacement for Hubble expected before the 2040s, the RFP states.

item.title: 两个皇帝与《辨谤略》
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

唐德宗贞元年间，唐次曾任礼部员外郎。后来因朝中人事牵连，被外放为开州刺史，在巴峡一带停留十多年，一直没有得到升迁。西川节度使韦皋曾上表请求任用唐次为副使，德宗却暗中命韦皋作罢。

唐次长期滞留偏远之地，心中郁结，于是搜集古代忠臣贤士因谗言受害、遭到放逐，甚至因此丧命，而君主仍不醒悟的事例，写成三篇《辨谤略》，进呈朝廷。

唐德宗读后十分恼怒，对左右的人说：“唐次这是把我比作古代的昏君，为什么这样自作比拟？”此后，唐次并未因此得到重用。

后来唐宪宗即位。一次，他在宫中读书，偶然看到唐次当年进呈的三篇《辨谤略》，读后却很欣赏。

宪宗对学士沈传师说，唐次所编的这些辨别谗谤的事例，做君主的人应当时时阅读。他又认为古书中类似事情还有很多，唐次搜集得并不完备，于是命沈传师继续扩充。

沈传师奉诏，与令狐楚、杜元颖等人分头搜集材料，从周代一直搜罗到隋代，把忠臣贤士遭受谗毁的事迹加以整理，最终扩充成十卷，题为《元和辨谤略》。

同样是唐次留下的三篇文章，德宗读后认为是在讥刺自己；到了宪宗手中，却被视为君主可以用来警惕谗言、检点政事的参考。

关键词: 
皇帝
栏目: 
史海漫步
作者: 
尺素笺

item.title: 吴冠中的党员身份：一个艺术家与时代的复杂关系
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

吴冠中是20世纪中国最具影响力的画家之一。他以鲜明的艺术个性、对形式美和现代艺术的公开辩护闻名，也以敢言著称。然而，在他大量自传、回忆和艺术文字中，有一件人生大事却很少被提及：1983年，64岁的吴冠中加入了中国共产党。

这件事本身并非秘密。相关官方履历明确记载吴冠中于1983年入党。但在吴冠中自己的许多回忆文字以及后来整理的部分年表中，这一事件并未得到与其他重要经历相称的篇幅。这种明显的轻描淡写，究竟意味着什么，至今仍值得讨论。

据吴冠中的同事、中央工艺美术学院教师余秉楠后来回忆，吴冠中在1983年正式入党之前，曾不止一次递交入党申请，但一直没有获准。1982年，余秉楠担任装潢系党支部书记，看到吴冠中再次提出申请后，积极推动此事，吴冠中的申请最终获得批准。

这一细节十分重要。

吴冠中并不是在组织动员之下被动入党，而是曾经主动提出申请，而且不止一次。仅凭这一事实，就很难简单地断言他“其实并不想入党”。至于他为什么希望加入共产党，则是另一个更复杂的问题。

理解这件事，需要回到吴冠中此前几十年的经历。

吴冠中出生于1919年，1940年代赴法国学习绘画，1950年回国。此后的中国美术界长期强调革命现实主义，艺术创作被赋予明确的政治功能。吴冠中的留学背景、对现代西方艺术的兴趣以及强调形式语言的艺术观念，与当时的主流文艺路线始终存在距离。

他的家庭背景也并不有利。土地改革以后，吴家被划为地主成分。回国后，他先后辗转于多所学校任教，直到1960年代才逐渐稳定下来。文化大革命期间，他同许多知识分子一样下放劳动，艺术创作受到严重限制。

真正的转折发生在1970年代末。

文革结束以后，中国文化界开始出现明显变化。思想解放逐渐展开，过去长期受到压制的西方现代艺术重新进入公共讨论。吴冠中也在这一时期迅速活跃起来。

1979年前后，他陆续发表《绘画的形式美》《关于抽象美》等文章，公开讨论形式、抽象和艺术规律。在今天看来，这些观点并不惊人，但在当时的中国美术界却具有很强的冲击力。

中国美术长期奉行“内容决定形式”的理论，绘画首先承担政治宣传和社会教育功能。吴冠中强调形式自身的审美价值，实际上触碰了当时美术理论中一个十分敏感的问题。

争论很快升级。

时任中国美术家协会主席江丰公开批评西方现代派艺术，并警惕美术界出现所谓“资产阶级自由化”倾向。1982年，江丰在有关会议上批评有人“竭力鼓吹西方现代派腐朽美术”，同时轻视革命美术。虽然讲话没有直接点名，但当时美术界普遍将吴冠中视为这一争论中的重要人物。

这使吴冠中的处境出现了一种微妙矛盾。

一方面，改革开放已经开始，中国正在重新接触世界现代艺术；另一方面，旧有的政治与艺术观念并未完全退出历史舞台。文革结束不过数年，人们对于政治运动的记忆仍十分新鲜。艺术争论随时可能越出艺术范围，重新成为政治问题。

正是在这样的环境里，吴冠中加入了共产党。

因此，讨论他的入党动机，如果只用“信仰”或者“功利”两个词来解释，都可能过于简单。

吴冠中完全可能真心希望得到一个被体制正式接受的身份。对于经历过1950年代政治运动和文化大革命的知识分子来说，政治身份从来不仅是一种观念表达，它也意味着安全感、社会认可和职业空间。

同时，他加入共产党，也并不意味着他因此接受了党内某些人主张的艺术理论。

1983年底，吴冠中在给友人的信中提到自己受命创作大型革命历史题材油画《井冈山》。他特别写道，这是有关方面“一再动员”之后，由自己这个“新党员”承担的一项“他们认为极重要的任务”。

这段文字颇有意味。

它至少显示，吴冠中对于这种政治任务式的艺术创作并没有表现出特别强烈的热情。他可以成为党员，却仍然坚持自己的艺术判断；可以接受体制身份，却未必认同体制内部关于艺术的一切要求。

这可能正是吴冠中最值得注意之处。

他不是一个能够简单归入“体制艺术家”或者“反体制艺术家”类别的人。他长期生活在中国的官方艺术教育体系中，在中央工艺美术学院任教，也担任过全国政协委员、全国政协常委；与此同时，他又不断批评中国美术中的僵化观念，强调艺术家的独立判断，并公开挑战长期占据主导地位的艺术理论。

1980年代以后，吴冠中的艺术声誉迅速上升。

他先后在香港、新加坡、日本和欧美举办展览，作品进入国际艺术市场。1991年获得法国文化艺术荣誉，1992年大英博物馆为他举办大型展览。他逐渐成为国际社会最熟悉的中国现代画家之一。

有人因此推测，吴冠中后来很少谈自己的党员身份，是担心这一身份影响海外艺术市场。

这种说法有一定想象空间，但目前缺少足够直接的证据。

吴冠中的党籍并非秘密，国内官方履历一直可以查询。如果要证明他刻意向海外隐瞒这一身份，还需要更直接的材料，例如本人书信、经纪人记录、海外展览策划文件或者收藏家的明确证言。仅仅因为他的自传较少提及党籍，还不足以证明这是为了维护作品价格。

更值得注意的问题其实是：吴冠中本人如何理解政治身份与艺术身份之间的关系。

他的老师吴大羽留下过一个意味深长的故事。

1956年，吴冠中到上海看望多年未见的吴大羽。临别时，吴大羽忽然问他：“你是共产党员吧？”

吴冠中回答：“不是。”

这一问一答后来被吴冠中本人写进回忆文章。

至于吴大羽为什么这样问，已经很难知道。有人把它解释为吴大羽察觉到吴冠中身上某种时代政治气息，但这只是后人的解释，不能当作吴大羽本人的明确判断。

然而这个细节确实具有某种历史象征意味。

27年以后，吴冠中真的加入了共产党。

从1956年的一句“不是”，到1983年的正式入党，中间横跨了反右、大跃进、文化大革命以及改革开放初期。对于吴冠中这样一代知识分子来说，这27年不仅是个人生命史，也是中华人民共和国政治与文化环境剧烈变动的一段历史。

吴冠中的选择不能脱离这种历史背景来理解。

他不是一个纯粹生活在画室中的艺术家，而是一个在政治高度介入文化的时代中成长、受挫、求生并最终成名的知识分子。

他可以批评僵化的艺术理论，也可以申请加入共产党；可以接受政协委员的身份，也可以坚持现代主义的审美趣味；可以承担革命历史题材创作，同时又把主要精力投入完全不同的艺术探索。

这些看似矛盾的行为，恰恰构成了那个时代许多知识分子的真实处境。

如果一定要寻找吴冠中1983年入党的“唯一动机”，很可能反而会把历史简单化。

现有材料能够证明的是：他曾多次申请入党；在受到艺术路线批评的时期终于获得批准；此后继续在体制内工作并取得越来越高的社会地位；但他的艺术观念并没有因此发生根本改变。至于其中究竟包含多少政治认同、多少现实考虑、多少安全感需要，今天很难替他作出最后判决。

历史研究最重要的，也许正是在这里停下来。

能够证明的，就说到能够证明的地方。

吴冠中晚年很少主动强调自己的党员身份，这个事实值得注意；但比猜测他的内心更有意义的，是看到一个艺术家如何在20世纪中国复杂的政治与文化环境中寻找自己的位置。

吴冠中的经历并不只是一个画家的个人故事。

它同时提醒后人：在一个政治、身份与艺术长期纠缠的时代，一个人的选择往往既不是简单的忠诚，也不是简单的投机。

有时候，那只是一个人在历史之中，为自己的艺术、生活与尊严寻找能够继续走下去的位置。

关键词: 
党员
艺术家
栏目: 
史海漫步
栏目重点发表: 
栏目头条
作者: 
余墨渡简

item.title: 1967年赴京“请示汇报”
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

1966年夏，全国开始“革命大串联”。红卫兵和学生可以免费乘坐火车、轮船，各地设立接待站，提供住宿和伙食。许多年轻人借此走出家乡，第一次见到北京、上海、武汉等大城市。

那一年我年纪小，没有赶上。

1967年初，大串联逐渐停止，各地接待站开始撤销。听着高年级同学讲述旅途见闻，我十分羡慕，总觉得错过了一次免费出门的机会。

没想到几个月后，我又找到了去北京的理由。

当时，无为县的群众组织已经分成两派。一派以县直机关干部和部分工人为主，设在县政府大楼；另一派主要由几所中学和师范学校的师生、县医院职工及少数机关干部组成，设在县工商联办公室，后来迁到无为中学。

我也和几个人组织了一个“战斗队”，平时印传单、贴标语，游行时扛着旗跟在队伍后面。

两派相比，我们这一边人数较少。县直机关干部和工人游行时队伍浩浩荡荡，而学生平时分散在各自家中，临时很难召集起来。拖拉机站和汽车队的工人又都有生产任务，不能随时参加活动。

为了寻找支持，1967年5月，我们几十人乘坐县汽车队的客车前往合肥。

省政府接待站先把我们安排在安徽工学院，后来又转到合肥工业大学教学楼住宿。那时接待任务很多，我们等了几天，也没有得到明确答复。

等待期间，我第一次见到了标准游泳池。一个同学兴奋地跳进水里，因为水浅，肚子重重拍在水面上，疼得半天直不起腰。

省里没有结果，有人提出，既然地方解决不了，不如直接到北京“向中央请示汇报”。

这句话正合我意。上一年的大串联我没有赶上，这一次终于有机会去北京了。

我们一共七个人，来自县卫生防疫站、水产公司、无为师范和几所中学。有人把我们带进合肥火车站，送上开往蚌埠的列车。

到蚌埠后，怎样继续北上成了问题。

我先和其他人分开，趁列车员不注意，上了一列开往徐州的火车。到达徐州时已是夜晚，我在车站外买了些吃的，一边等同伴，一边寻找继续北上的办法。

那天夜里，我遇到一个和我年龄相仿的北京学生。他衣服整齐，却独自坐在车站外。他告诉我，父母受到批斗并被关押，他只好离开北京，到南方寻找亲戚，却不知道究竟能投奔谁。

我们在屋檐下聊了一阵。后来各自靠着墙睡去。

五月底的徐州，前半夜还很热，后半夜却冷了下来。我只穿着一件春秋衫，冻得牙齿直打颤。天刚亮，我在车站外吃了一碗小米粥和几根油条。那是我第一次吃小米粥，觉得格外香。

其他六个人后来也赶到了徐州。他们买的是蚌埠附近一站的短途票，却一直坐到了终点。当时车上很少查票，这种“买短坐长”的办法并不少见。

我们继续分头找车。

我和水产公司的老吕上了一列开往济南的火车。到达济南后，车站广播通知去北京的旅客上车，我们十分高兴，立即跟着人流登车。

列车最终只开到天津西站。

老吕下车另找办法，我则留在车上。途中我认识了几个河南开封的学生，他们手里有北京市中学生返京证明。我跟着他们，准备设法混上进京列车。

空车后来调到天津北站。几个学生翻过围墙，到附近水塘游泳，我只能留在车厢里等他们。傍晚列车又开到天津站，他们说，车可能要到第二天凌晨才出发。

晚上九点多，我走出车站，独自在天津街头转了一圈。

劝业场的大钟已经接近十一点，海河大桥和街边霓虹灯仍然亮着。商店大多关门，街道上行人很少。因为担心错过火车，我没有走得太远，很快又回到车站，在原来的车厢里打瞌睡。

半夜，我忽然听到站台上传来熟悉的家乡口音。原来另外几个人也到了天津，正为怎样进北京发愁。

我告诉他们，开封学生有返京证明，可以跟着一起上车。

第二天凌晨，列车员先把所有人赶下车重新检票。开封学生的证明上有十来个人的名字，我们便一个接一个跟着上车。人数显然多了，但同行的邢庭华站在车门口一边帮着数人，一边同列车员纠缠，最后竟把大家都拉了上去。

火车驶离天津，沿途只停了廊坊一站。

1967年6月6日清晨五点，我们到达北京站。东边太阳刚刚升起，远处就是天安门广场。第一次来到北京，我们都十分兴奋。

首都接待站设在劳动人民文化宫附近。工作人员把我们安排到东直门外左家庄住宿。那里是一片刚建成不久的住宅，接待站发给每个人草席、毯子和二十多天的餐券。

据说要等二十多天，才轮得到我们接受接待。

住宿和吃饭解决后，我便开始在北京四处游览。

我身上带着一张北京交通图，是二哥上一年参加大串联时买回来的。每天吃完早饭，我揣上一个馒头便出门，有时乘公共汽车，有时步行，晚上再回到左家庄。

我先去了天安门广场。

当时广场上除了天安门城楼的毛主席像，东西两侧还竖着马克思、恩格斯、列宁和斯大林的画像，南面靠近前门处竖着孙中山画像。人民英雄纪念碑以南还有一大片没有铺地砖的黄土地，零星栽着几棵小松树。

我还去了人民大会堂、革命历史博物馆、前门和东交民巷。

故宫当时没有开放，颐和园、天坛和北海公园可以游览。我没有去长城，因为听人说路远，也没有什么可看的。后来大家一起去颐和园，在那里留下了一张合影。

北京街头到处可以看到文革留下的痕迹。

在南池子附近的英国驻华代办处外，悬挂着一个纸扎的外国人像，头上戴着高帽。院内有人隔着窗户向外看。后来不久，那里发生了火烧英国代办处事件。

苏联大使馆附近的道路上，地面用油漆写着很大的“反修路”三个字。使馆门外站着中国军人，院子里也不时有人向外张望。

我绕着故宫走了一圈，看见中南海附近一处住宅门前贴满大字报，地上散落着许多纸张。有人说那里是刘少奇的住处。门外还挂着几双高跟鞋，作为批判王光美“资产阶级生活方式”的展品。

那时北京正在修建地铁，大片古城墙和城门被拆除。东直门城楼尚未完全拆掉，许多解放军战士正在工地施工。我站在一旁看了很久，心里觉得十分可惜，甚至想，如果能把这些砖瓦木料运回无为，重新建起一座城楼，该有多好。

当时的北京并不像我想象中那样整洁。六月风沙很大，东直门大街虽然宽阔，两边建筑却显得灰暗，行道树也不多。市民穿着大多朴素，街上很少看到鲜艳颜色。

同行几个人除了去过一次天安门，大多数时间留在接待站研究怎样汇报。我则天天早出晚归，几乎把能够到达的地方都走了一遍。

二十多天后，终于轮到我们接受接待。

水产公司的汪开科说，所有人都去，行李无人看管，便让我这个年龄最小的留下。

结果，他们去见了什么人，说了什么，得到什么答复，我后来都不知道。我名义上是到北京“请示汇报”的，最后却连汇报会都没有参加。

接待结束后，中央接待站发给我们返程车票，还发了一些毛主席像章和宣传材料。我们收拾行李，乘火车返回安徽。

离开北京前，我到王府井买了一双塑料凉鞋和一个军用水壶。回程在蚌埠换车时，装凉鞋和宣传材料的袋子被人偷走。那些沿途收集的大字报、传单和油印小报，也一并丢失了。

1967年6月这次赴京，名义上是“向中央请示汇报”。对当时的我来说，却更像是抓住了革命大串联的尾巴，完成了一次不用购买车票、也不用承担食宿费用的北京旅行。

资料来源：谢同裕《文革中的赴京请示汇报是一次免费旅游》

文革

item.title: Democrats' midterm victory was historic. These numbers show just how big it was.
item.description:
Midterms tend to be backlash elections, and the president’s party almost always loses seats when voters return to the polls to judge his performance in office. 

But not all midterms are created equal. 

On Tuesday, Democrats comprehensively routed their Republican rivals, regaining control of the U.S. House, U.S. Senate and statehouses across the country. Along the way, they shattered a series of decades-long Republican winning streaks and notched several historic firsts. 

So just how big was this year’s blue wave (or “blue tsunami”)?  

The full scale and scope of the Democratic Party’s seismic victory is still coming into focus as officials tally every last vote. But here are some key numbers to help you put it into perspective: 

Winning the House

26: the average number of House seats the president’s party has lost in midterm elections since World War II (pre-2026)

40+: the projected number of House seats that will flip to Democrats in 2026, once all the votes are counted 

About 255: the projected size of the new Democratic House majority — the largest since 2008, and possibly since 1992

6.8 percentage points: the Republican popular vote margin in their 1994 and 2010 House midterm victories

13 points: the projected Democratic popular vote margin in their 2026 House midterm victory 

1974: the last time either party won their House popular vote by that much in a midterm election

More than 100: the number of Democratic women who will serve simultaneously in the House — a historic first 

Flipping the Senate 

4: the average number of Senate seats the president’s party has lost in midterm elections since World War II (pre-2026)

9: the number of Republican Senate seats that have either flipped to Democrats in 2026 (Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, Texas) or could flip once all the votes are counted (Alaska, Mississippi)

55-56: the projected size of the new Democratic Senate majority — the largest since the early 2010s

2014: the last time a party — the Republicans — flipped 9 Senate seats in a midterm election

1958: the last time a party flipped more than 9 Senate seats in a midterm election

12 points: Trump’s average margin of victory in 2024 in the nine states where Democrats flipped or could still flip a Republican Senate seat this year

1986: The last midterm in which more than two Senate seats flipped in states where the president won by double-digit margins two years earlier

At least 17: the number of senators from both parties who will be replaced in the chamber after the 2026 midterms — the largest turnover since 1980 

70: the average age of this year’s departing senators

At least 15: the number of senators from both parties who will be under 50 when they’re sworn into office in January 2027 — up from eight previously

Closing the ‘governor gap’

7: the number of Republican governorships that have either flipped to Democrats in 2026 (Iowa, Ohio, Georgia, Nevada, Texas) or could flip once all the votes are counted (Alaska, Kansas)

As many as 31: the number of governorships that Democrats could control once all the votes are counted

2011: The last time Democrats controlled a majority of governorships

About 75%: the percentage of Americans who will live in states with Democratic governors after the 2026 midterms 

How voters shifted

63%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said they disapprove of how Trump is handling his job as president

54%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said they “strongly” disapprove of how Trump is handling his job as president

37%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said they approve of how Trump is handling his job as president — the lowest midterm approval of any president since at least 2006

91%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said government corruption was a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress

62%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said Trump prioritizes his own personal interests over the country’s interests

89%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said the cost of living was a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress

66%: the percentage of exit poll respondents who said Trump’s policies have worsened economic conditions in the U.S. 

+15 percentage points: An early estimate of how much better Democrats performed nationwide in 2026 vs. 2024 (via the New York Times)

+20 points: An early estimate of how much better Democrats performed in the South in 2026 vs. 2024 

+28 points: An early estimate of how much better Democrats performed with Latino voters in 2026 

+32 points: An early estimate of much better Democrats performed with young voters (ages 18-29) in 2026 vs. 2024

Turning Texas blue

2.6 percentage points: Democrat James Talarico’s final lead in the polls, on average 

About 12 points: Talarico’s actual margin of victory over Republican Ken Paxton in the 2026 midterm election

1988: The last time Texas elected a Democratic senator

5.26 million: The number of votes Joe Biden received in Texas in the 2020 presidential election

5.45 million: The number of votes Talarico has received in Texas in the 2026 midterm election — the most ever for a Democrat

64%: The estimated percentage of Texas independent voters that Talarico won in the 2026 midterm election 

70%: The estimated percentage of Texas Latino voters that Talarico won in the 2026 midterm election 

73%: The estimated percentage of young voters (ages 18-29) that Talarico won in the 2026 midterm election

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/article/democrats-2026-midterm-rout-was-big--really-big-here-are-the-numbers-that-prove-it-225923613.html

item.title: 快讯：韩9月国际收支经常项目顺差614.6亿美元
法国爆发新一轮全国罢工 当局部署7万警力戒备
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

法国将于11月5日举行新一轮跨行业罢工及示威活动，工会主要要求提高工资、改善公共服务待遇，并反对政府削减预算。法国内政部长努内兹表示，全国将部署约7万名警察和宪兵，以维持秩序并防范可能发生的暴力事件。

此次罢工涉及教育、铁路、航空及医疗等多个行业。法国教育部预计，公立小学教师罢工比例约为17.54%。法国国家铁路公司多个工会联合发动罢工，部分地区列车及巴黎郊区快铁将减班或延误，但高速铁路预计仍有约九成班次正常运行。巴黎地铁、公交和有轨电车服务预计基本正常。

航空交通管制人员也将参与罢工，部分机场航班可能受到影响。巴黎公立医院工会则反对政府拟议的医疗预算削减措施。

努内兹表示，警方将保障合法示威活动，同时对暴力违法行为采取强硬措施。此次抗议正值法国政府面临财政紧缩压力之际，工资待遇与公共支出成为劳资双方争议焦点。

关键词: 
法国
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 国会易主会否导致特朗普对华政策受限？白宫回应：总统外交政策从未出于政治动机
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

美国民主党在星期二（11月3日）的中期选举赢得了国会众议院和参议院的控制权，国会政治版图的改变是否可能导致华盛顿对北京的政策或谈判空间受限？美国白宫副新闻秘书安娜·凯莉（Anna Kelly）星期三对美国之音表示，唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）总统的外交政策决定“从未出于政治动机”，而是以“人民利益和国家安全”为准则。

美国选民星期二以选票决定了新一届国会参众两院控制权的归属。尽管部分地区的计票工作仍在持续，美国之音（VOA）与多方已经作出预测，判定民主党在此次选举中赢得了国会参众两院的掌控权。

虽然中国议题或美中关系在此次选举中并不是左右选情的重要议题，许多候选人的胜负也与他们在中国议题上的立场无关，但民主党掌控国会后，增加了与共和党籍的唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）总统和行政当局的抗衡。

与此同时，特朗普总统将在两个星期后，到深圳出席亚太经济合作组织（APEC）非正式领导人峰会，并在会议的间隙与习近平再次举行两人今年第三次双边峰会。而美中之间的贸易休战临时协议也将在两个月后期满。

美国国会山政治版图的改变是否会对未来的美中关系以及特朗普与中国国家主席习近平的互动产生影响？

白宫副新闻秘书安娜·凯莉星期三以电邮回应美国之音的置评请求。她表示，“特朗普总统的外交政策决定从未出于政治动机。我们的总司令将始终以美国人民的最佳利益和我们的国家安全为行动准则。”

两党对华立场分歧不大

总部位于布鲁塞尔，从事贸易信用保险和政治风险保险的欧洲信用保险集团Credendo在中期选举后的一篇分析文章中指出，美国两党在对华关系上其实分歧并不大，两党都视北京为潜在的对手和威胁，因此也都支持在对华关系上采取限制性的策略，包括限制对华出口先进技术，限制对华投资，但同时又希望避免让美中贸易紧张关系进一步升级。

文章指出，新国会可能会尝试改善与美国传统盟友的关系。美中贸易关系的缓和可能会继续，尽管超级智能（通常称为人工智能，AI）的发展可能成为两大国之间的主要争议点。

此外，该文指出，美国国会两党中仍有绝大多数人支持发展美台关系，支持美国向台湾提供先进武器和防务援助。因此，民主党掌控国会后，预计国会将继续强力推动落实遭特朗普搁置的重大对台军售项目，并敦促总统不要在与北京的谈判中将台湾问题当作筹码。

特朗普对华政策空间恐受限

路透社在选后一篇分析报道中则认为，民主党掌控国会两院可能让特朗普的对华政策空间受限。

报道说，中国是美国最大的竞争对手。中国与特朗普达成的一项贸易休战临时协议明年1月份到期后，北京可能会寻求利用特朗普政治上的脆弱处境来增强自身筹码。但与此同时，在国会的密切注视下，北京想要争取特朗普让步或许会变得更加困难。

路透社援引澳大利亚科琳娜经济咨询公司（Corinna Economic Advisory）的经济学家索尔·伊斯莱克（Saul Eslake）的话说，习近平会意识到，特朗普的权威可能因此次选举结果而大为削弱，并很可能会考虑如何利用这一点。

特朗普此前致力于改善与习近平的关系。然而，由民主党掌控的国会可能会限制他为未来协议提供“甜头”的能力。

法国外贸银（Natixis）亚太区首席经济学家艾丽西亚·加西亚-埃雷罗（Alicia Garcia-Herrero）向路透社表示，民主党人不太可能让特朗普在与北京达成协议时拥有完全的自主权。她指出，民主党此前就曾批评特朗普与习近平的会晤在超级智能等关键议题上缺乏实质性成果。

她补充道，由民主党掌控的国会更有可能支持加强技术出口管制，并对超级智能和半导体领域的供应链进行更严格的审查。这将削弱特朗普在涉及这些高增长领域时做出让步的灵活性。

叶望辉：新国会需维持对华战略资金

前白宫副总统国家安全副顾问叶望辉（Steve Yates）在美国保守派智库传统基金会（The Heritage Foundation）创办运营的新闻与评论网站“每日信号”（Daily Signal）上撰文说，选民或许并未关注对华政策，但本届政府已制定了一套连贯的对华战略；下一届国会将必须为该战略提供资金并予以维持。2026年版《国防战略》提出，要“通过实力而非对抗”来威慑中国，其核心在于沿“第一岛链”构建“拒止型”防御体系。

叶望辉指出，民主党掌控国会后，目前由共和党人设立的众议院中国问题特设委员会的存废将是一大看点。该委员会并非永久性机构，其存在仅基于众议院的规则安排，且当前的授权将于本届国会结束时到期。

在来自密歇根州的共和党籍委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔（John Moolenaar）的领导下，该委员会因推动旨在打击贸易犯罪的《PAIL法案》（该法案已于8月在众议院获得通过）而赢得了美国制造业界的赞誉。目前，一个行业联盟已向两党领导人提出请求，希望在下一届国会中延续该特设委员会的授权。

叶望辉指出，由一个特设委员会专注中国的行为比通过一项立法更有意义。

叶望辉认为，在台湾及其盟友问题上，美国国会两党均保持支持态度。来自两党的参议员已敦促政府就一项总额140亿美元的待定军售案发出通知；此外，国会两院的国防法案均提出延续“太平洋威慑倡议”，并扩大与台湾的安全合作。相比之下，对此的民意支持则较为薄弱：若中国大陆对台湾采取军事行动，仅有38%的美国民众支持派遣美军介入，这一比例低于2021年的52%。

美国对华政策不会有大波动

美国前国防情报局代理局长戴维·谢德（David Shedd）认为，政策延续性的基础，是两党对中国所构成威胁的共同关切。布鲁金斯学会研究员、前白宫国家安全委员会中国事务主任秦江南（Jon Czin）也得出了类似结论，但对华盛顿应采取哪些具体政策，他质疑两党究竟有多大共识。

两人的分析指向一个区别：国会可以增加压力、推动立法并质疑行政部门的决定，却未必能够改变一位仍然主导对华关系的总统的政策方向。

“我不认为美国对华政策会出现太大波动，”秦江南选前在接受美国之音采访时说。

谢德选前接受美国之音采访时则表示，众议院和参议院“在应对中国所代表的威胁方面，确实存在非常强烈的两党合作趋势”。

谢德预计，总统将继续寻求与北京进行建设性互动，而国会仍会关注安全威胁。

民主党虽然赢得了国会两院的主导权，但是美国的外交政策仍然时总统的权责。因此分析人士认为，特朗普总统仍然将保持与习近平的私交并维持美中之间发展互利平稳对等的关系。

即使面对民主党在中期选举中展示的“蓝潮”或“蓝色海啸”，特朗普总统在社媒X平台上贴文强调，面对国会，总统拥有“否决权”，意即如果未来民主党掌控的国会通过他不喜欢的议案，他仍可以行使否决权。而推翻总统的否决，国会需要三分之二的绝对多数。

中国当局对民主党在中期选举中大胜的结果，反应审慎。

“中期选举是美国内政，”中国外交部发言人毛宁星期三在北京举行的例行记者会上表示。“中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好、落实好两国元首重要共识，加强沟通，妥处分歧，拓展合作，构建基于尊重、公平、对等的中美建设性战略稳定关系。”

关键词: 
对华政策

item.title: 美国选出了历史上首位穆斯林参议员，这条路走得并不容易
item.description:
一个令人沮丧的事实是，仇视穆斯林的偏见一直是美国政治中的污点。 密歇根州立大学上个月进行的一项民意调查发现，超过38%的受访者表示，如果候选人是穆斯林，他们投票支持此人的可能性会有所降低或大幅降低。其中，表示支持可能性会大幅降低的人占了大多数。 同一项调查显示，民主党州长候选人领先共和党对手12个百分点。 相比之下，埃尔-赛义德的领先幅度还不到3个百分点。 而密歇根州拥有全美第二多的阿拉伯裔美国人口，其中许多人信奉伊斯兰教。 这种明显的差距，似乎揭示了美国社会在接纳不同群体方面仍然存在的局限。 可他还是赢了。 在这个社会分裂不断加深的时代，埃尔-赛义德的胜利提醒我们，政治归根结底仍然是人与人之间的事情。 每个政治人物都有自己的经历和理念。他们必须一个接一个地说服选民，让人们暂时放下彼此之间的差异，转而关注共同的梦想。

item.title: 美中两军举行危机沟通会议 商讨降低军事冲突风险
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国战争部11月3日宣布，美中两军于11月2日至3日在华盛顿举行危机沟通与预防工作组年度会议，讨论降低双方军事冲突风险及改善紧急沟通机制。

美方代表为战争部负责中国、台湾与蒙古事务的首席主任辛西娅·卡拉斯，中方代表为解放军国际军事合作办公室美洲大洋洲局副局长王玮大校。

美国战争部声明指出，双方一致认同推进务实沟通措施、降低美中军事风险的重要性，并就拓展危机管理渠道、建立便捷有效的沟通方式交换意见。

美方表示，未来数月将继续与中国军方讨论关键防务议题。

美中两军近年来曾因双边关系紧张而中断部分交流，随后逐步恢复接触。此次会议旨在加强危机管控，减少双方军机、军舰在台湾海峡及南海等敏感地区活动时发生误判或意外升级的风险。目前双方尚未宣布签署新的正式协议。

 

关键词: 
美中关系

item.title: Key races yet to be called include nail-biters in Colorado and Mississippi
item.description:
Democrats on Tuesday comprehensively routed their Republican rivals, regaining control of the U.S. House, U.S. Senate and statehouses across the country.

It was one of the most lopsided midterm performances in modern U.S. history.

Coming into the night, Republicans held 53 of the Senate's 100 seats; Democrats held 45. To wrest back control of the Senate, Democrats needed a net gain of at least four seats. As at 11:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, the Democrats had won 54 Senate seats to the GOP's 44 — and they could wind up winning as many as 56 once all the votes are counted in Alaska and Mississippi, where key races have yet to be called.

In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in one of the most closely watched races. James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in the Lone Star State since 1988. 

Annie Andrews beat GOP Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina to flip a Senate seat. In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeated incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins, putting an end to her three-decade tenure. Sen. Jon Ossoff comfortably won reelection in Georgia. Other Senate seats to flip to the Democratic Party included Roy Cooper in North Carolina, Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Josh Turek in Iowa and Adam Hamilton in Kansas.

In the 435-seat House, the GOP held 218 seats; the Democrats held 214. To retake control of the House, Democrats needed a net gain of three seats. The AP said early Wednesday that they had exceeded that figure; the latest estimates show that the party is on track to win its largest majority since 2008. And there are still seats it could flip, including the one held by Republican incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert, a staunch Trump ally, whose race against Democrat Eileen Laubacher remains tight.

There were also 36 gubernatorial races and numerous ballot measures to keep an eye on. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor-elect. El-Sayed will be America's first Muslim senator.

President Trump, whose approval ratings are at or near all-time lows, distanced himself from mounting Republican losses in a post on Truth Social on Tuesday night.

"I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" Trump wrote. "Thank you for your attention to this matter."

The president later said he was willing to work with Democrats while also suggesting he wouldn't hesitate to use his veto powers.

Trump also blamed Fox News, declaring that the conservative news network "bears the responsibility" for the GOP's sweeping midterm election losses.

In a post on X, Vice President JD Vance said blamed the GOP on the war with Iran.

"The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," he wrote. "The reason we lost is the war."

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/live/midterms-2026-live-updates-election-day-voters-head-to-the-polls-as-democrats-look-to-flip-gop-control-of-the-house-and-senate-110000715.html

item.title: 美国联邦医疗保险D部分保费预计2027年平均上涨50%，在开放投保期重新比较方案才是上策
item.description:
KFF预计，2027年联邦医疗保险D部分独立处方药保险计划的平均月保费为51美元，较2026年的34美元上涨50%。八项全国性计划的月保费预计约为6至204美元。 对未获得低收入补贴的独立处方药保险参保人来说，若不调整现有计划，76%的人将在2027年支付更高保费，涉及约1040万人。大多数参保人还将面临免赔额。 今年开放投保期为10月15日至12月7日，调整将于2027年1月1日生效。KFF表示，约430万名受益人当前参加的计划将在2026年底终止。

item.title: 梅拉尼娅将接待俄乌代表 乌克兰援助点遇袭40人死亡
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·川普定于11月5日在白宫接待俄罗斯和乌克兰代表，介绍她协助促成的乌克兰奥列什基局部停火及人道主义行动。此前为期六天的停火安排使约800名平民得以撤离。乌克兰总统泽连斯基已授予梅拉尼娅一级奥尔加公主勋章，表彰她提供的人道主义援助。

与此同时，乌克兰官员表示，俄罗斯11月2日袭击扎波罗热地区科米舒瓦哈一处设在学校内的援助点，截至4日已造成至少40人死亡，另有数十人失踪。俄国防部称袭击目标为乌克兰军人，目前尚无法独立证实。

美国斡旋的俄乌美三方会谈定于11月10日至11日在阿布扎比举行，重点讨论战后安全、局势降级及人道主义措施。

尽管美国中期选举导致国会易主，俄罗斯仍表示希望川普继续推动和平。泽连斯基也强调，美国总统仍有能力协助结束战争。

关键词: 
梅拉尼娅
俄乌战争
栏目: 
要闻
